errata.notes: SETCLIENTID operation is NFSv4.0 specific operation. NFSv4.1 uses CREATE_SESSION or BACKCHANNEL_CTL operation for setting backchannel parameters.
Mentioned RFC 2203 (and also its updates RFC 5403 and RFC 7861) does not have any enum rpc_gss_svc_t. Instead it has enum rpc_gss_service_t and all enum values are lowercase.

Section 2 of RFC 5662 presents the NFSv4.1 protocol definition in the XDR language of RFC 4506, which it cites normatively. Lines that begin with "%" are not part of that language. The "%" prefix is an rpcgen convention: rpcgen copies the rest of the line verbatim into its generated C output. An XDR compiler that implements RFC 4506 rejects these lines. A code generator for another target language, such as Rust or Python, has no use for the C they contain.

Most of the "%" lines in Section 2 carry only comments and can become ordinary XDR comments without changing the protocol. The block quoted above carries C preprocessor directives and a C typedef that import authsys_parms from the host's RPC headers. Without that block, the extracted XDR does not define authsys_parms, which callback_sec_parms4 uses for its AUTH_SYS arm. The extracted XDR does not define AUTH_NONE, AUTH_SYS, or RPCSEC_GSS either. The corrected text supplies these definitions in XDR, taken from RFC 5531 Section 8.2 and  Appendix A.

RFC 4506 Section 4.15 permits a union discriminant of type "int", "unsigned int", or an enumerated type. The discriminants of nfs_cb_argop4 and nfs_cb_resop4 are declared with the bare type "unsigned", which is not an XDR type. rpcgen accepts the bare type because C does, but an XDR compiler that implements RFC 4506 strictly rejects both declarations.

The corrected text declares both discriminants as nfs_cb_opnum4, as RFC 5662 already does for nfs_argop4 and nfs_resop4 with nfs_opnum4, and as RFC 7863 does for these two unions. The encoding on the wire does not change, because every nfs_cb_opnum4 value is non-negative and an enum encodes as a 4-byte integer, as unsigned int does.
